newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - March 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - March 25.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- CRAVEN TO QUIT AS CHAIRMAN OF MORGAN

One of the City's leading bankers, Sir John Craven, is to resign as chairman of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, the City bank involved in the Nichola Horlick and Peter Young affairs. He is said to have been disappointed by the two incidents. Young's losses are costing Deutsche Bank, Morgan's German parent, 380 million stg. Several Morgan staff have left and the Imro regulator is expected to inform the bank of a proposed one million stg fine.
-- LEICESTER TO JOIN LEAGUE OF FOOTBALL FLOATERS

Premiership football club Leicester City is intending to float on the stock market this summer which could value the club at between 40 and 50 million stg. Leicester said that it had not decided whether to float on the Stock Exchange or the Alternative Investment Market. Funds from the float will be used to develop the Filbert Street stadium, buy new players and develop the club's youth policy.
-- REED 320 MILLION DOLLARS FOR U.S. DATA GROUP

Anglo-Dutch publisher Reed Elsevier has announced it is buying MDL Information Systems, an American publisher of data-bases for chemical and biological research, for 320 million dollars. A member of Reed's executive committee, Paul Vlek, said the offer was fair and that he thought the company was worth it. MDL also publishes software for exchanging scientific data in the life sciences and chemical industries and made pre-tax profits of 11 million dollars last year.
THE TIMES
-- U.K. DEFICIT OF 14 MILLION STG THE BEST FOR 11 YEARS

Figures show that Britain achieved its best trading performance for more than a decade last year. The balance of payments have been returned to virtual balance on the back of resilient exports and record earnings from invisible trade. Prime Minister John Major has seized on the figures as proof that Britain is booming due to Conservative policies and people's hard work. He claimed that the world had put its faith in Britain's goods and services and that the election of a Labour government would put this success at risk.
-- LYONNAISE AND SUEZ SHARES UP ON TALK OF MERGER

Reports of a possible merger has led to a sharp rise in the shares of Lyonnaise des Eaux, the French utilities group, and Cie de Suez, the holding company. Analysts said they expected an agreement by the end of the month. The merger has excited political, financial and media speculation in Paris as the deal would create an international giant. This would give rise to tensions within French industry and between France and Belgium, where Suez controls an important utilities group.
-- SAUDI PRINCE SETS HIS SIGHTS ON SIX LONRHO PRINCESSES

Prince al-Waleed bin Talal is close to buying six of the hotels in the Princess chain from Lonrho for 350 million stg. Prince al-Waleed is expected to merge the hotels with Fairmont Hotels in which he owns 50 per cent. The deal does not include the Princess hotels in Bermuda and Barbados. The purchase is the latest step of global purchases which have cost the prince billions of pounds stg.
THE GUARDIAN
-- CADBURY FAILS TO SHIFT VOTING

Research by Pirc, the corporate governance consultancy, showed that the average vote for annual meeting resolutions have risen by only two percentage points to 39 per cent. This suggests that the voting performance of Britain's biggest shareholders has improved only fractionally since Sir Adrian Cadbury put institutional investors at the centre of enforcing better boardroom standards three years ago.
-- TOON ARMY FAITHFUL KICK CITY JEREMIAHS INTO TOUCH

Newcastle United football club has announced it hopes to raise 54 million stg from the 193 million stg floatation, to use to repay debts. Some City analysts say that the shares were fully valued and that the recent passion for the sector was dwindling. There is also concern that Newcastle's earning potential is limited by St James' Park, its 36,000 capacity stadium. However, the ten per cent of floatation set aside for non-City investors was seven times oversubscribed.
-- BULLION FIRM JILTED AS GOLD WEDDING IS CALLED OFF

The world's oldest bullion dealer, Mocatta, has been rejected by three suitors, Dresdner Bank, Canada's Bank of Nova Scotia and Dutch group ABN Amro. The Standard Chartered subsidiary is thought to have a price-ticket of 200 million stg. It is thought the cost structure at Mocatta may have played a part in all three decisions, as did the negative effects of the Sumitomo scandal on the whole of the metal trading industry.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- KRUPP-THYSSEN TRUCE SETS STAGE FOR PEACEFUL MERGER

Krupp-Hoesch has announced the withdrawal of its hostile takeover bid for Thyssen. This comes after week-long talks mediated by business leaders and politicians. Both companies have pledged to "explore possibilities for co-operation". The merger would create a rival to British Steel. Krupp say the merger would create cost savings in other areas such as engineering and automotive components.
-- FERRARI FACTOR POWERS INCHCAPE

According to car distribution group Inchcape, sales of Ferraris are booming in Britain and provide evidence of a buoyant consumer economy. Imports rose by 20 per cent last year. Inchcape also said that sales of other top-of-the-range cars, such as BMWs, Mercedes and Chysler Cherokee jeeps, were buoyant. The luxury car boom is one of a series of indicators showing that higher-value products are selling well. Figures from Champagne Information Bureau show that champagne shipments to the U.K. were back to the same level as during the eighties boom.
-- 270,000 STG IN PERKS FOR CHIEF OF NEW CABLE AND WIRELESS GROUP

Documents issued to shareholders show that chief executive of Cable and Wireless Communications, C&W's proposed new five billion stg cable group, Graham Wallace, has been given 100,000 stg on joining the company and will receive a 170,000 stg bonus this year in addition to his basic salary. The documents also reveal that the process of merging C&W's Mercury subsidiary with three cable operators will cost 35 million stg in fees, to be paid to City lawyers and advisers.
